system_summary.purpose: Make the identification, understanding, organisation, intervention and revision of end-to-end work coherent while preserving distinctions between warranted knowledge, legitimate/effective action and observed consequences.
system_summary.environment: Organisations and cooperating or partly autonomous partners, with variable work, incomplete observation, resource constraints, human judgement and competing legitimate interests.
system_summary.objects_and_state: Needs, cases/work objects, obligations, real work, resources, responsibilities, process representations, observations, hypotheses, interventions and received consequences. Their states are related but not interchangeable.
system_summary.actors: Recipients and affected people; performers and professionals; analysts/modellers; owners/functional managers; sponsors; technical/support actors; autonomous partners. Roles may be combined where competence and authority permit.
system_summary.operational_meaning: People and systems perform tasks, commit resources, make decisions, exchange messages and alter real records/objects/obligations. Models support these acts but do not create authority or establish their success.
system_summary.control_form: A conditional relation network with recurring inquiry, alternative representations and interventions, concurrent work where justified, and exception/unsafe-continuation interrupts. No universal fixed stage order is prescribed.
system_summary.minimal_coherent_form: A meaningful purpose and boundary; enough evidence of actual work to support the decision; an intelligible shared account; an existing or explicitly agreed capable authority; proportionate action or reasoned non-action; observation of consequences and a route for correction. No mandatory diagram, engine, mining system, maturity assessment or BPM office.
system_summary.validation_status: The components have distinct source support; this exact composition is an analytical construction tested by counterexamples, not an empirically validated universal BPM programme.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Lightweight process stewardship
alternative_configurations.TRIGGER: Small, understandable work with limited interdependence and reversible consequences.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Use case examples and a short purpose/responsibility account, existing management authority, proportionate change or non-action and direct outcome review.
alternative_configurations.OMITTED_BY_DEFAULT: Formal architecture, simulation, mining, maturity assessment, BPM office, execution engine and low-code platform.
alternative_configurations.ESCALATION_TRIGGER: Material hidden dependencies, repeated misunderstanding, consequential constraints or scale exceeds the cheap path.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT_CONDITION: No recurring decision need or the protected function is supplied adequately elsewhere.
alternative_configurations.COST: Time for shared understanding and evidence remains; lightweight does not mean undocumented harm.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Structured repeatable process
alternative_configurations.TRIGGER: Stable case identity, repeated tasks and a credible benefit from shared representation or automation.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Choose a purpose-fit procedural representation and selectively automate stable portions while preserving meaningful exceptions and external completion.
alternative_configurations.OMITTED_BY_DEFAULT: Formal simulation, complete enterprise architecture and exhaustive automation unless their triggers hold.
alternative_configurations.ESCALATION_TRIGGER: Resource uncertainty may justify simulation; unstable cases may require the knowledge-work configuration.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Case regularity disappears or maintenance/exception burden dominates.
alternative_configurations.COST: Model maintenance, adoption support and interface/recovery obligations.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Goal- and case-oriented professional work
alternative_configurations.TRIGGER: Work evolves with evidence and expertise; a prespecified activity sequence would distort consequential judgement.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Represent goals, case facts, responsibilities and binding constraints; leave qualified actors discretion over the path.
alternative_configurations.OPTIONAL_ADDITION: EBPM-073 only when interacting formal constraints justify checking and the encoding/history obligations are met.
alternative_configurations.OMITTED_BY_DEFAULT: A compulsory single sequence or model of every possible expert action.
alternative_configurations.ESCALATION_TRIGGER: Recurrent harmful variation may justify stronger standard constraints or specialist review.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT_CONDITION: A specialised case mechanism has no recurring consumer or a simpler practice supports equivalent judgement.
alternative_configurations.COST: Dependence on expertise, review and communication; discretion can remain inconsistent.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Negotiated interorganisational process
alternative_configurations.TRIGGER: Independent organisations jointly determine the received outcome.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Negotiate interfaces and commitments, reconcile meanings and retain each organisation’s authority boundary.
alternative_configurations.OMITTED_BY_DEFAULT: A presumed network-wide owner with unilateral powers or unrestricted data sharing.
alternative_configurations.ESCALATION_TRIGGER: Disputed effects, new partners or incompatible incentives require renewed agreement rather than merely a larger diagram.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT_CONDITION: The shared dependency or commitment ends.
alternative_configurations.COST: Negotiation, incomplete information and potential strategic behaviour remain.

alternative_configurations.NAME: Evidence-intensive decision support
alternative_configurations.TRIGGER: A consequential question exceeds cheap observation and adequate data/models exist.
alternative_configurations.MECHANISM: Use simulation, mining or causal analysis as explicitly bounded evidence for accountable decisions.
alternative_configurations.OPTIONAL_ADDITION: EBPM-052 for checked modelling assistance; EBPM-072 for governed local delivery when its separate trigger holds.
alternative_configurations.OMITTED_BY_DEFAULT: Autonomous self-authorising redesign; EBPM-053 remains unresolved and is not a prerequisite.
alternative_configurations.ESCALATION_TRIGGER: Model error, missing causal variables, drift or unobserved external effects trigger renewed inquiry or a non-analytical alternative.
alternative_configurations.RETIREMENT_CONDITION: The analysis has no actionable consumer or a cheaper method resolves the decision.
alternative_configurations.COST: Data preparation, model checking, review and possible false confidence.

domain_models.name: Process identity and purposes
domain_models.question: What received result makes this work a meaningful unit of intervention, and where does responsibility end?
domain_models.objects: Initiating needs, cases or work objects, activities, dependencies, recipients, completion claims and material external burdens.
domain_models.actors: Performers and recipients supply distinct accounts; sponsors and authorised owners decide scope and priorities; partners retain autonomous commitments.
domain_models.evidence: Complete-case examples, receiving-side outcomes, unmet needs and interfaces. An organisation chart contributes authority information but does not establish process identity.
domain_models.decisions: Identify a meaningful case/episode and completion rule; select which process merits attention; include or explicitly bound material effects; resolve or preserve competing purposes.
domain_models.operation: Change work allocation, commitments or the selected intervention scope. A portfolio or architecture only informs these acts; it does not perform them.
domain_models.feedback: Complaints, displaced delay, ambiguous closure and changed strategy can reopen purpose or boundary decisions.
domain_models.limits: Not all work has one stable repeated case. Open-ended inquiry may be managed through goals and responsibilities without heavy process standardisation. Expanding the boundary indefinitely is also a cost.
domain_models.coupling: A purpose criterion becomes operative when those receiving the outcome can inform an actor able to choose or change the work; a diagram alone cannot supply either condition.

domain_models.name: Discovery evidence and performed work
domain_models.question: Which aspects of actual work are warranted by which observations, and what remains unknown?
domain_models.objects: Prescribed procedures, remembered accounts, observed cases, event records, variants, informal coordination and disagreements.
domain_models.actors: Analysts elicit and compare accounts; practitioners and recipients validate or challenge them; data custodians explain recording conditions.
domain_models.evidence: Interviews expose reasons but can idealise practice; workshops reveal disagreement but can suppress weaker voices; observation exposes action but samples selectively; logs scale observation but inherit system boundaries.
domain_models.decisions: Choose evidence channels by the uncertainty that matters; sample relevant variants and missing participants; record unresolved disagreements rather than manufacture a single consensual as-is truth.
domain_models.operation: Conduct walkthroughs, observe cases, inspect documents and data generation, and return the representation to relevant participants. Discovery changes inquiry and shared understanding, not necessarily work itself.
domain_models.feedback: A workaround, recipient complaint or failed prediction can trigger new observation and boundary revision.
domain_models.limits: No channel is automatically ground truth. The inspected textbook discovery chapter was abstract-only, so detailed methodological claims here rely on primary cases and the other inspected sources.
domain_models.coupling: Evidence has a consumer: modellers, analysts and redesign decision-makers. The consumer must know whether a statement describes a prescription, a sample observation or an unresolved inference.

domain_models.name: Representation and communication
domain_models.question: What must these users distinguish, and which representation supports that purpose at acceptable cost?
domain_models.objects: Activities, events, decisions, control/data/resource relations, goals, cases, constraints and abstraction levels.
domain_models.actors: Domain participants judge meaning; modellers maintain representations; technical specialists check defined syntax and execution semantics.
domain_models.evidence: Comprehension and modelling experiments, domain walkthroughs and formal/specification checks establish different kinds of quality. A notation specification does not establish real-world accuracy.
domain_models.decisions: Choose a narrative, table, procedural model, decision representation or case/declarative form; decide whether a representation is communicative, analytical or intended for execution.
domain_models.operation: Participants explain and challenge model meanings; tools may validate syntax or encoded behaviour; separately authorised execution changes real work.
domain_models.feedback: User misunderstanding, semantic discrepancy, constraint conflict and changed work trigger selective revision.
domain_models.limits: The 7PMG null-result experiment does not prove guidelines useless, but defeats automatic sufficiency. Declarative satisfiability does not validate omitted obligations. DMN 1.5 was verified at version-record level only; detailed clause compliance is not claimed.
domain_models.coupling: Representation supports communication only when users can interpret consequential distinctions. Agreement on the picture may leave decision authority or exceptions unresolved.

domain_models.name: Performance and causal analysis
domain_models.question: Which mechanism produces the observed outcome, and how much can the available evidence justify changing it?
domain_models.objects: Elapsed time, processing effort, queues, resources, arrivals, case mix, rework, handoffs, costs and outcome distributions.
domain_models.actors: Analysts define measurements and comparisons; performers explain hidden work; owners decide resource and redesign interventions.
domain_models.evidence: Separate elapsed time from active work, description from prediction and prediction from causal effect. Simulation requires resource, arrival, routing and state assumptions; repeated simulation runs do not remove model error.
domain_models.decisions: Locate plausible bottlenecks or error mechanisms; compare alternative explanations; decide whether a cheap observation, calibrated model or experiment is needed.
domain_models.operation: Measure complete cases, inspect rework causes, build and check quantitative models where warranted, then make a separately authorised intervention.
domain_models.feedback: Unexpected outcomes, case-mix changes, resource changes or poor predictive calibration reopen the diagnosis.
domain_models.limits: High utilisation is not a universal objective. The inspected causal-discovery method uses a specific model and benchmark setting; real interventions need their own assumption checks and comparisons.
domain_models.coupling: A correct performance distinction only matters when its implications reach an actor able to change capacity, routing or working conditions; measured outcome change remains a separate claim.

domain_models.name: Redesign and alternatives
domain_models.question: Which intervention changes the actual failure mechanism at acceptable transition and ongoing cost?
domain_models.objects: Current work, alternative arrangements, protective functions, dependencies, case classes, resources and transition commitments.
domain_models.actors: Owners, performers, specialists and affected recipients compare alternatives; sponsors authorise resources and disruption.
domain_models.evidence: An as-is baseline, explicit mechanism hypothesis and relevant comparison. Practitioner support for a heuristic supplies plausibility and use experience, not a universal causal effect.
domain_models.decisions: Choose among removal, resequencing, parallel work, coordination, pooling, segmentation, better information, automation, organisational repair and no intervention.
domain_models.operation: Actually alter tasks, responsibilities, information or resources; preserve necessary controls and manage transition.
domain_models.feedback: Adverse cases, failed adoption or absent outcome improvement can require reversal, a different alternative or retention of the original work.
domain_models.limits: Elimination can remove a control; parallelisation adds synchronisation; pooling creates queues and larger failure domains; segmentation can disadvantage hard cases. Radical and incremental change remain alternatives.
domain_models.coupling: The proposed mechanism, authorised change and its effect must all be evidenced. A more elegant to-be diagram is not an implemented improvement.

domain_models.name: Organisational governance and capability
domain_models.question: Who can make consequential process decisions, with what competence, resources and accountability?
domain_models.objects: Decision rights, sponsorship, process ownership, functional responsibilities, support capabilities, incentives and escalation relations.
domain_models.actors: Sponsors allocate commitments; process owners coordinate outcomes; functional and professional managers retain explicitly assigned powers; BPM specialists enable or govern within their mandate.
domain_models.evidence: Actual decisions, resolved conflicts, resource commitments and demonstrated skills. Policies, titles and self-rated stages are supporting artefacts, not sufficient evidence of capability.
domain_models.decisions: Choose a governance configuration and support level; decide which capability gaps warrant investment; resolve cross-functional conflicts.
domain_models.operation: Delegate powers, supply resources and training, negotiate commitments and act on escalations.
domain_models.feedback: Persistent blocked decisions, local bypass, poor outcomes despite high ratings or changing dependencies reopen governance choices.
domain_models.limits: The six-element framework describes strategic alignment, governance, methods, IT, people and culture; it does not prove that all must grow through identical stages. Central, local and federated arrangements have different failure modes.
domain_models.coupling: Responsibility becomes operative through exercised authority and practical ability. Participation requires influence on decisions, not merely attendance.

domain_models.name: Human discretion, exceptions and responsibility
domain_models.question: When should a person follow, vary, challenge or stop the ordinary process, and who judges that departure?
domain_models.objects: Case circumstances, professional knowledge, binding constraints, optional work, workarounds, reasons and affected-party consequences.
domain_models.actors: Practitioners exercise bounded expertise; authorised reviewers adjudicate consequential departures; recipients and workers can challenge harmful designs or interpretations.
domain_models.evidence: Case narratives, observed exceptions, recipient experience and analysis of the protected function of both the rule and its workaround.
domain_models.decisions: Permit a justified departure, correct a misfit, preserve a necessary standard or reject unsafe circumvention.
domain_models.operation: Change the case path, supply expert judgement, stop unsafe action or resolve an exception while retaining outstanding responsibilities.
domain_models.feedback: Repeated justified exceptions can change a process; recurrent harm or unequal discretion can justify stronger constraints or training.
domain_models.limits: Neither universal conformance nor universal celebration of workarounds is retained. Visibility can enable accountability and also surveillance. The social-work criticism is abstract-only, limiting claims about its detailed empirical design.
domain_models.coupling: The system must let people communicate exceptional facts to someone able to act. An override button without authority, competence or actual control is not meaningful discretion.

domain_models.name: Enactment, automation and external effects
domain_models.question: How does a design become functioning work, and what remains the organisation’s responsibility outside software?
domain_models.objects: Operational roles, training, systems, interfaces, deployments, actual cases, external effects and partial failures.
domain_models.actors: Owners coordinate enactment; technical teams implement bounded systems; performers and support teams make them usable; recipients and partners establish received consequences.
domain_models.evidence: Readiness and real-use observations, adoption, receiving-side completion and unresolved exceptions. Technical availability does not establish any of these by itself.
domain_models.decisions: Select a suitable technical or non-technical implementation, authorise external operations and determine how interrupted work will be resolved.
domain_models.operation: Perform work, communicate commitments, transfer objects or alter records. This is where real objects and relations change, not merely internal representations.
domain_models.feedback: Non-adoption, manual repair, interface changes, failed delivery or harmful automated decisions reopen design and governance.
domain_models.limits: BPM-level composition identifies recovery obligations without supplying the full workflow-engine algorithmic lane. Low-code usability evidence is not proof of non-specialist competence or safe deployment.
domain_models.coupling: A deployable workflow is a technical artefact. A functioning organisational process additionally needs skills, authority, resources, coordination and outcome evidence.

domain_models.name: Monitoring, adaptation and differentiated revision
domain_models.question: What observations can change which decisions, and how are descriptions, work and outcomes kept distinct?
domain_models.objects: Indicators, baselines, assumptions, model versions, actual practices, complaints, interventions and evaluation judgements.
domain_models.actors: Analysts supply signals; authorised owners or professionals decide action; performers and recipients supply evidence missing from system logs.
domain_models.evidence: Decision-linked measures, comparison with the intervention hypothesis and independent routes for omitted work to challenge the model.
domain_models.decisions: Investigate, act, refrain, retire a control, revise a model, change work or reconsider the objective. These are distinct decisions with different authority requirements.
domain_models.operation: Change resources, tasks or commitments where authorised; a representational correction alone does not alter operations.
domain_models.feedback: The revision itself is evaluated. Criteria may be reconsidered openly but not silently rewritten to declare the previous intervention successful.
domain_models.limits: Feedback does not prove convergence or self-authorisation. A dashboard with no capable consumer is not an adaptive process, while indiscriminate alerts can consume the capacity needed to act.
domain_models.coupling: Learning is a two-way relation: observations inform decisions and consequences revise the evidence model. Exceptions may interrupt any ordinary phase rather than waiting for a lifecycle stage.

domain_models.name: Cross-organisational and contemporary consequences
domain_models.question: How can process coordination and innovation remain accountable across autonomous actors and new technical capabilities?
domain_models.objects: Shared outcomes, interface meanings, commitments, disclosure boundaries, environmental/social effects, analytical models and delegated automation.
domain_models.actors: Autonomous organisations negotiate commitments; affected people supply consequences; analysts and tool builders do not acquire network authority by integration.
domain_models.evidence: Field and design-science cases, surveys, technical benchmarks and research agendas are kept distinct. Reused datasets and case programmes do not create independent replications.
domain_models.decisions: Negotiate governance, determine necessary information sharing, include material impacts and select bounded use of intelligence or AI.
domain_models.operation: Coordinate real interorganisational commitments, test interventions and deliver consequences under separately justified authority.
domain_models.feedback: Partner disputes, displaced harm, data-semantic changes or failed AI/analytics assumptions trigger review.
domain_models.limits: The 2026 agentic manifesto is an agenda, not operational assurance. Sustainability readiness is not measured environmental benefit. The September 28–October 2, 2026 conference is future relative to the cut-off and is not treated as completed evidence.
domain_models.coupling: Interoperability, intelligence and visibility are enabling capabilities only. They do not by themselves settle interests, grant authority or establish benefit.

nodes.NAME: Industrial-engineering and quality-process antecedents
nodes.PROBLEM: Fragmented tasks, unmeasured total elapsed time and quality problems across functions.
nodes.MECHANISM: Measurement and whole-process attention, critically contrasted with isolated task rationalisation.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Davenport and Short explicitly locate process thinking in quality-management and industrial-engineering discussions.
nodes.LIMITS: This is documentary evidence of their engagement, not a comprehensive history of Taylor, Deming or all quality schools; cited earlier books were not independently read.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Measurement and end-to-end attention persist, while purely local task optimisation is challenged.

nodes.NAME: Office information systems and workflow antecedents
nodes.PROBLEM: Coordinate office work across people, information and organisational activities rather than automate isolated calculations.
nodes.MECHANISM: Early office-system models, information-control nets and Petri-net-related representations; renewed workflow-management development in the 1990s.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: The inspected 2013 survey connects early work by Ellis, Holt and Zisman and systems such as Officetalk and SCOOP to the technical workflow branch.
nodes.LIMITS: Historical account inspected at survey level. Those 1970s original works and full product implementations were not independently inspected; the record establishes a qualified antecedent, not a new primary-source priority claim.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Formal process representations and enactment support persist in process-aware information systems, alongside rather than in place of organisational approaches.

nodes.NAME: Radical re-engineering formulation
nodes.PROBLEM: Technology accelerates inherited fragmented work without reconsidering its structure.
nodes.MECHANISM: Reconstruct work around outcomes and cases; challenge handoffs and entrenched task divisions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Hammer’s practice argument makes structural redesign a prominent alternative to automating existing tasks.
nodes.LIMITS: Selected success stories do not identify a universal effect; disruption, skills and authority are not solved by the slogan.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Redesign remains a branch of BPM rather than a universally replaced or universally required stage.

nodes.NAME: IT and business process redesign
nodes.PROBLEM: Functional systems and local optimisation obstruct received outcomes.
nodes.MECHANISM: Relate strategic purpose, process selection, baseline measurement, IT possibilities and prototyping.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Davenport and Short include interindividual, interfunctional and interorganisational processes, multiple objectives and work-life/learning concerns.
nodes.LIMITS: Their broad enthusiasm for IT-driven redesign exceeds what selected cases can causally establish.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Cross-boundary purpose, selective intervention and sociotechnical implementation remain useful; technology alone is not enough.

nodes.NAME: Critical reconstruction of BPR claims
nodes.PROBLEM: Novelty and organisational reform claims may be fashionable, ambiguous or unrealistic.
nodes.MECHANISM: Critically distinguish claimed originality and assumptions from defensible organisational mechanisms.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Biazzo supplies a contemporary critical stance rather than later retrospective praise alone.
nodes.LIMITS: Only the abstract and bibliographic record were accessible; detailed arguments and underlying evidence are not attributed beyond that access.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: This study narrows radical-as-default and avoids a clean BPR-to-BPM progress story.

nodes.NAME: Situated work and dual-use process descriptions
nodes.PROBLEM: Formal workflow descriptions misfit actual coordination yet remain organisationally useful.
nodes.MECHANISM: Distinguish enactment guidance from accounting/contractual uses of process records.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Dourish’s PF2 analysis explains why discrepancies and workarounds need interpretation rather than blanket removal of formal records.
nodes.LIMITS: The earlier empirical text was not retrieved; the 2001 analysis is not a new independent replication.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Provides a documented cross-disciplinary challenge to diagram-as-truth and ceremony stripping that ignores consumers.

nodes.NAME: Information-systems/workflow-centred BPM
nodes.PROBLEM: Workflow products and proliferating acronyms lack clear conceptual/formal foundations.
nodes.MECHANISM: Use explicit process designs, enactment/management/analysis and formal methods for process-aware systems.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Van der Aalst, ter Hofstede and Weske describe BPM as extending classical workflow in their systems-centred account.
nodes.LIMITS: Their declared focus on structured repeated cases is not a universal definition of all organisational BPM.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: The technical branch remains important but is not permitted to erase organisational or knowledge-work branches.

nodes.NAME: Redesign heuristics and practitioner appraisal
nodes.PROBLEM: Redesign advice is dispersed and lacks a structured account of mechanisms and trade-offs.
nodes.MECHANISM: Organise task, resource, information and organisational redesign patterns and elicit practitioner use/impact judgements.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Separates concrete options such as elimination, resequencing, parallelism, pooling and task composition.
nodes.LIMITS: Practitioner ratings are not controlled effects; implementation cost is not the operational-cost measure.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Heuristics survive conditionally with explicit control, skill, dependency and coordination prerequisites.

nodes.NAME: Declarative and case-oriented flexibility
nodes.PROBLEM: Rigid activity sequences cannot adequately support evolving cases and exceptions.
nodes.MECHANISM: State constraints or case information and let qualified actors choose admissible actions; analyse encoded conflicts and history compatibility.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Provides alternatives to a single prescribed sequence and a bounded formal consistency mechanism.
nodes.LIMITS: Correct encoding, complete histories and operational legitimacy remain separate; case orientation and declarative formalism are related alternatives, not identical.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Knowledge-intensive BPM retains selection between procedural, case and constraint-based forms.

nodes.NAME: Model-quality heuristics and empirical challenge
nodes.PROBLEM: Complex or poorly labelled models can obstruct communication and analysis.
nodes.MECHANISM: Use modelling guidelines and assess their effects on actual tasks and users.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: 7PMG offers practical heuristics; later experiment provides a null-result challenge to automatic benefit.
nodes.LIMITS: A fifty-element guideline is not a universal theorem; student tasks and language-specific positive studies have limited transfer.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Purpose-fit modelling retained; guideline compliance is not accepted as proof of quality.

nodes.NAME: Organisational capabilities and governance
nodes.PROBLEM: BPM cannot be sustained by methods and IT without strategic, organisational and human capacity.
nodes.MECHANISM: Differentiate strategic alignment, governance, methods, IT, people and culture; examine exercised ownership and contextual configurations.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: The six-element account and owner field study recover substantive organisational dimensions; 2026 taxonomy distinguishes governance choices.
nodes.LIMITS: Framework relevance and taxonomy usefulness do not establish a universal successful hierarchy.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Context-fit configuration replaces mandatory central-office or role-count assumptions.

nodes.NAME: Simulation for tactical and short-term decisions
nodes.PROBLEM: Static models and naive simulations misrepresent resources, current state and uncertainty.
nodes.MECHANISM: Model and validate process performance; reconstruct current state and distinguish stochastic from model error.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: 2026 experiments refine a bounded forecasting task and expose sharpness/coverage and model-misfit trade-offs.
nodes.LIMITS: Retrospective as-is fit is not intervention-effect validation; unmodelled delays and attributes remain material.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Simulation remains an optional, assumption-sensitive decision method.

nodes.NAME: Event-based process intelligence
nodes.PROBLEM: Actual execution evidence is dispersed and technical analytics may not lead to action.
nodes.MECHANISM: Use event data for discovery, conformance and enhancement while linking technical, individual, group, organisational and ecosystem levels.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Documents an adjacent field and its interaction with BPM’s improvement purposes.
nodes.LIMITS: Logs are selective; case identity and data quality matter; mining results do not confer intervention authority.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Later synthesis must reconcile shared mechanisms without claiming BPM invented or subsumes process mining.

nodes.NAME: Broader lifecycle and contextual BPM synthesis
nodes.PROBLEM: Tool reduction and disconnected methods obscure the wider management task.
nodes.MECHANISM: Relate identification, modelling, analysis, enactment and monitoring with context, purpose, people and appropriate technology.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Comprehensive survey, ten principles and textbook organisation show a broad established field.
nodes.LIMITS: The textbook itself was accessed at record/contents and a chapter abstract, not read cover-to-cover; underlying primary evidence carries stronger claims.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Lifecycle categories are retained as connected concerns, not a compulsory serial pipeline.

nodes.DATE: 2016; criticism updated 2024 and challenged by 2026 association
nodes.NAME: Maturity-model validity debate
nodes.PROBLEM: Capability ratings and prescriptive stages may lack empirical validation.
nodes.MECHANISM: Review evidence and distinguish dimension-specific diagnosis from a universal ladder or outcome proxy.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Critical reviews identify limits; recent ESG-readiness associations prevent claiming the complete absence of positive evidence.
nodes.LIMITS: Cross-sectional readiness is not causal impact; full 2026 methods remain inaccessible.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Maturity assessment remains useful but easily gamed, not proof of achieved performance.

nodes.NAME: Longitudinal workflow implementation evidence
nodes.PROBLEM: Success-only reports conceal adoption failures and mixed outcomes.
nodes.MECHANISM: Track intended processes through implementation and compare observed/modelled performance where possible.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Preserves the distinction between 25 intended and seven implemented processes.
nodes.LIMITS: Historical cohort, survivor selection and incomplete model validation limit attribution and current-platform transfer.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Technical deployment and business outcome improvement remain separate acceptance claims.

nodes.NAME: RPA, low-code and citizen development
nodes.PROBLEM: Organisations seek inexpensive automation and wider participation in application delivery.
nodes.MECHANISM: Interface automation and model-based development lower some construction barriers; support and governance address operational dependencies.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Documents technical continuity and the organisational work needed around decentralised development.
nodes.LIMITS: Vendor/tool categories are not economic-effectiveness evidence; usability populations and abstract-only current studies constrain transfer.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Selective automation and governed participation survive; automated-as-improved does not.

nodes.NAME: Responsible, Green and interorganisational BPM
nodes.PROBLEM: Efficiency-only and single-organisation perspectives omit affected people, environmental effects and autonomous partners.
nodes.MECHANISM: Include material impacts, negotiated governance, disclosure/meaning boundaries and accountability.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Surveys, conceptual work and design-science cases expand the questions asked of process design.
nodes.LIMITS: Reporting readiness, normative desirability and model usability are not proof of environmental or network outcome improvement.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Broader consequences are retained while conflicts remain explicit rather than declared balanced.

nodes.NAME: Workaround-driven improvement cycle
nodes.PROBLEM: Recognising misalignment does not automatically identify a suitable intervention.
nodes.MECHANISM: Investigate recurring workarounds and connect root-cause categories to alternative improvements.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Adds a structured response to the process/work discrepancy without automatically endorsing the workaround.
nodes.LIMITS: Selected settings and related earlier cases limit independent replication and prevalence claims.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Feeds discovery, redesign and evaluation while preserving competing responses.

nodes.NAME: LLM assistance and agentic BPM research
nodes.PROBLEM: New models can generate process artefacts, but organisational action and revision need stronger assurance.
nodes.MECHANISM: Benchmark model creation and feedback; propose a research programme for more autonomous process management.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Separates measurable modelling tasks from open questions of accountable autonomy.
nodes.LIMITS: Benchmarks are not actual-work truth or deployment outcomes; a manifesto is not a validated system.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_CONTINUITY: Assistance is assumption-sensitive; autonomous process self-revision remains unresolved.

genealogy.method: Dates identify the cited formulation, not an asserted first-ever invention. Documentary influence is distinguished from shared problem ancestry, import, criticism and analytical convergence. Earlier works named only inside an inspected source are not silently treated as independently read.
unresolved_relationships: A complete causal genealogy from every industrial/quality founder to contemporary BPM is not established; this packet uses explicit documentary connections rather than resemblance.
No direct Dourish-to-2026-workaround influence is claimed without documentary support.
Organisational BPM, BPR and workflow-centred BPM coexist; a single BPR-to-BPM replacement edge is rejected.
BPMN, EPC, decision and case representations are alternatives with different purposes, not a universal sequence of superior notations.

criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Radical redesign may repackage familiar ideas, underestimate organisational realities and mistake selected successes for a general method.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Biazzo’s inspected abstract advances a critical argument; early practice accounts are selected cases; the later longitudinal programme includes non-implementation.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Preserve outcome and cross-boundary reconstruction while selecting change scale and preserving continuity.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Longitudinal implementation selection remains a material limit, not an excuse to redefine failed projects out of scope.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Radical-as-default rejected; radical change retained only as an option.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No credible universal BPR failure percentage is established here.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S025 methods/cases; S035 guiding principles; S041 pp. 53–55
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Official or logged accounts can omit essential coordination and the meaning of work.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Dourish reanalyses the PF2 print-work case; contemporary workaround research examines goal/process misfit.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Triangulate sources and preserve discrepancy as evidence; do not replace one supposedly perfect source with another.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: The 2026 workaround cycle supplies a structured response but remains case-based and genealogically related to earlier studies.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Unqualified log-ground-truth rejected; discovery evidence retained with sampling and observability limits.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Frequency and generality of particular omitted-work patterns remain unknown.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S009 guidelines; S010 methods/results/limitations; S044 evaluation
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Recommended modelling form does not reliably produce better models or comprehension for every user and task.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: S010: 21 students across two executions, 42 models, guideline task second; no significant benefit on tested outcomes. S044: narrow developer task comparison supports a different language intervention.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use guidelines as heuristics and assess purpose/user/task fit rather than infer quality from compliance.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Low-code usability findings concern different users and interventions, not a replication or direct refutation of the null study.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Universal fifty-element threshold superseded; complexity management retained but easily bureaucratised.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Small samples, order effects and limited occupational transfer constrain inference.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: BPMN 2.0.2 §§1.1, 2.1, 13.1; CMMN scope; S041 dual-use account
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A syntactically or executably valid model need not describe actual work or establish organisational completion.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: BPMN distinguishes modelling/execution conformance and limits operational semantics; a formal account can serve an accountability consumer while misfitting enactment.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Keep representation, execution, authority and business completion as distinct evidence claims.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Richer case and declarative forms address some rigidity, not the entire model/reality gap.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Notation-conformance-as-truth rejected.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Model-to-implementation and business-effect correspondence require local evidence.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S014 requirements; S026 abstract; S042 constraints/change sections
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Prespecified paths can undermine professional judgement; unrestricted flexibility can omit obligations or permit harmful behaviour.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Knowledge-intensive process analysis, critical social-work abstract and declarative formal/prototype account.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Retain bounded discretion and choose procedural, case or declarative alternatives by case uncertainty and constraints.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Formal consistency checks help within encoded semantics but do not validate omitted professional obligations.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Universal prescriptive standardisation rejected; constraint checking domain-specific.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Empirical evidence for broad organisational benefits of declarative deployment is weak.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S017 simulation pitfalls; S027 outcome evaluation; S030 responsibility; S041 work accounts
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A local or convenient measure can reward delayed, displaced or harmful outcomes; full utilisation is not universally desirable.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Analytical model limits and observed divergence between formal work accounts and performed work; no universal causal estimate of gaming is claimed.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use outcome-valid plural measures, case-mix interpretation and bottleneck/capacity analysis where warranted.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Responsible BPM extends the affected-party question without proving a universal optimisation rule.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Single-metric sufficiency and maximum-utilisation universalism rejected.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Protected values and acceptable trade-offs need legitimate local determination.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S017 pitfalls; S018 §§current state, uncertainty, evaluation
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A simulation may be precise about the wrong state, resource behaviour or demand regime; stochastic replications omit model error.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: 2026 comparison of current-state initialisation with warmed-up simulation and state-conditional uncertainty models.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Calibrate against relevant observations, separate uncertainty types and test sensitivity to current-state and demand assumptions.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: The contemporary extension improves bounded forecasting questions, not proof that future interventions will work.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Simulation retained as assumption-sensitive, not compulsory.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Observation incompleteness and future structural change remain.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S002 Rank Xerox caveat; S019 causal model/evaluation; S027 limitations
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Temporal sequence, prediction and before/after improvement do not by themselves identify an intervention effect.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Early authors acknowledge concurrent change; causal execution research uses a synthesised dataset and two open benchmarks under model assumptions.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Specify the intervention mechanism, comparison and causal assumptions; preserve evidence-insufficient outcomes.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Causal discovery is a documented import, not a universal cure for confounding or missing variables.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Causal restraint strongly retained; specific inference methods assumption-sensitive.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Actual organisational intervention effects remain setting-specific.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S016 practical assessment and objections, printed pp. 202–203 (PDF pp. 10–11), including Table IV
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Redesign heuristics can conflict: task integration violates segregation, centralisation adds delay and fewer participants can remove needed coordination.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: 25-practitioner survey and qualitative objections, not independent controlled tests of every heuristic.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Preserve distinct dependency, skill, authority and control prerequisites for each option.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: No later source in this bounded corpus establishes a universally dominant heuristic combination.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Heuristics retained conditionally; blanket control/human elimination rejected.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Interactions and transfer costs require target evidence.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S020 field findings; S021 governance framework; S027 organisational implementation conditions
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: An owner can be accountable without the authority or resources needed to influence cross-functional work.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Field study of owners and contemporary governance design framework.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Examine exercised decision rights, resource access and escalation, preserving functional/professional limits.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Context-aware governance supports alternatives rather than one universal hierarchy.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Nominal ownership is ceremony, effective authority is retained.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Comparative causal evidence among governance configurations is limited.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S022 review; S023 §8; S040 structured abstract
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Maturity models have weak validation, rigid paths, self-report bias and prescriptions that may not improve outcomes.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Reviews identify validation limits; 2026 Poland survey of 287 enterprises reports cross-sectional associations with ESG reporting readiness.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Use dimensions diagnostically and test the proposed capability investment against actual needs and outcomes.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: The new association does not overcome confounding, national transfer or readiness-versus-impact limits.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Maturity scoring useful but easily gamed; score-as-success is not a general property.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Independent longitudinal predictive and intervention validity remains incomplete.

criticism_ledger.LOCATOR: S024 survey limitations; S026 abstract; S030 responsibility; S041 work/accountability
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Participation, culture and transparency can become managerial control that suppresses judgement and shifts burdens.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: 733-response municipal culture survey is associational; critical and conceptual sources expose contrary mechanisms.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE: Make participation consequential, preserve challenge, and limit visibility to justified use.
criticism_ledger.LATER_FINDINGS: Responsible BPM supplies normative distinctions rather than demonstrated universal safeguards.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Predictable low-consequence work with redundant effort and no displaced protected function.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Variable demand, rare severe harm, vulnerable recipients or costly recovery.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Identify protected outcomes and compare savings with variability, failure exposure and distributional effects; do not optimise an aggregate that hides a protected loss.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Selective slack and protective checks with efficient routine handling.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A nominal safety exception lacks capacity or difficult cases are excluded from performance reports.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Reduced slack and fewer checks can increase tail delay, failure exposure and unequal burden.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Slack, protective checks and distributional evaluation consume capacity and may slow routine cases.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Stable repeated tasks with known constraints and costly avoidable variation.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Knowledge-intensive cases, incomplete information or contextual professional judgement.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Can the consequential decision be specified correctly in advance, and what does deviation protect or endanger?
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Standard constraints and routine paths with competent, reviewable exception handling.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Exceptions require impractical approval or the binding constraints are themselves incomplete.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Uniform prescribed paths can suppress expert judgement or mishandle exceptional cases.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Discretion requires expertise and review and can produce inconsistent or unaccountable decisions.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Local changes with evidence of negligible cross-boundary effects.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Shared queues, partner dependence or burden shifting.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Trace receiving-side time, effort and risk; qualify local claims when external consequences cannot be observed.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Local autonomy within negotiated interface and outcome commitments.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: The dominant actor defines success while the harmed partner cannot report or contest costs.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Local optimisation can transfer waiting, rework or risk to another actor.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Wider outcome accounting and cross-boundary coordination cost time and can dilute local decision speed.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Consequential decisions need traceable evidence and legitimate accountability.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Sensitive cases, employee-level inference or unnecessary disclosure.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which information changes a legitimate decision, who needs it and can less identifying evidence suffice?
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Purpose-limited access, aggregate learning and a route for affected-person challenge.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Aggregation hides harm or individually detailed data is reused for unannounced appraisal.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Detailed visibility can become surveillance, disclosure or punitive measurement.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Restricting visibility can reduce diagnostic detail or make responsibility harder to establish.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: The existing structure cannot meet purpose and incremental repair repeatedly fails.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Current service is critical, uncertainty is high or local repair plausibly suffices.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare structural inadequacy with transition risk, reversibility and the cost of waiting.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Piloted or staged replacement with protected continuity and explicit evaluation.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Dual operation doubles burden, hidden dependencies remain or the fallback is retired before adoption.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Radical change can disrupt ongoing cases, tacit knowledge, legitimacy and adoption.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Incremental continuity can preserve structural defects and forego a larger warranted gain.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Stable, well-observed tasks with reliable interfaces and bounded effects.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Ambiguous decisions, frequent exceptions, unstable interfaces or professional judgement.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Does the automated mechanism preserve the decision’s required information, authority and response to abnormal cases at lower total cost?
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Automated routine support with genuinely capable human exception handling.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Humans retain responsibility but lack context, time, skill or ability to override.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Automation adds integration, maintenance and exception costs and can amplify flawed decisions.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Human judgement and adaptable handling can be slower, less consistent and more expensive per routine case.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Shared dependencies, scarce expertise or cross-unit commitments need common decisions.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Local contexts differ and central delay impedes responsive work.
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Which decisions have cross-unit externalities and which can be delegated without losing necessary coverage?
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Federated decision rights and shared support with explicit local scope.

internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: The discriminator requires evidence from the actual process; this corpus does not supply universal thresholds or a single scalar ordering.

COSTS.FIRST_POLE_COST: Central governance can introduce bottlenecks and suppress context-specific knowledge.
COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Local initiative can duplicate work and create incompatible dependencies or unsupported applications.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Simple work or users/tasks better served by examples, narratives or tables.

COSTS.SECOND_POLE_COST: Simplification can lose explicit semantics, conceal dependencies or remove a needed accountability record.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Reversible low-cost changes or time-sensitive harm require timely action.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Irreversible consequences or confounded observations demand stronger evidence.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: A department halves its recorded handling time by releasing incomplete cases to the next team; the recipient waits longer.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Compare complete-case elapsed time, downstream repair and received result rather than the first department’s stopwatch.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Reject an unqualified end-to-end improvement claim; consider better handoff information or retaining local work instead of rewarding displaced effort.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Receiving-side evidence shows no extra burden and a better final outcome, in which case the local change may be accepted within that boundary.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Invented case, not a published experiment or effect-size estimate.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: An official model omits informal coordination that resolves conflicting customer information before a case ID exists.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Walk through actual cases with performers and recipients; compare activity before registration with system records.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Revise the discovery account and investigate the informal function before automating or suppressing it. The log alone cannot disprove the work.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Evidence shows the coordination has no useful function or causes greater harm; then redesign or remove it rather than canonise the workaround.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Invented test inspired by, but not equated with, the PF2 literature.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: A practitioner pauses a standard route because new case facts show that the routine decision would harm the recipient.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Assess competence, authority, the protected constraint and actual consequence of the pause; compare both rule compliance and departure.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: A justified manual exception can be a successful process response, not a failure merely because it reduces throughput.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: The pause lacks a defensible purpose, exceeds authority or produces greater avoidable harm; revise the exception policy or support.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: No medical, legal or safety protocol is prescribed; this is a neutral hypothetical test.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: RPA increases the number of decisions completed per hour, but the decision rule wrongly rejects a class of eligible recipients.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Separate execution accuracy from decision validity and inspect outcomes by affected class, including manual appeals.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Reject automation-as-improvement; stop or constrain the harmful operation through authorised actors and repair the decision mechanism.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Independent evidence validates the decision rule and shows improved received outcomes without displaced harm.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Invented test; not an allegation about a named RPA deployment.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: An organisation has complete process maps, named owners and high maturity ratings, yet unresolved cross-functional decisions and poor outcomes persist.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Trace a real decision through evidence, authority, resources and action; test whether assessment dimensions explain the observed inability.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Do not add paperwork merely to raise the score. Use a focused capability/authority diagnosis or conclude the assessment is unhelpful.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: The artefacts demonstrably support needed decisions and the poor outcome comes from a separately identified external constraint.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Invented case; reviews and surveys do not establish that all mature-looking organisations fail.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: An exploratory team works on unique evolving questions with no stable repeated case structure.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Ask whether standard routing would support a real repeated decision or simply force uncertainty into invented categories.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Heavy standardisation and a mandatory engine are inapplicable. Use goals, responsibilities, constraints and proportionate shared learning.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Stable recurring subwork emerges and evidence shows that a simple standard path would prevent a recurring error.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Non-trigger test, not a claim that all knowledge work is unmodellable.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: A simulation calibrated to ordinary demand recommends staff reduction just as case complexity and backlog increase.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Reassess current-state, resource and case-mix assumptions; distinguish narrow simulation intervals from trustworthy out-of-regime forecasts.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Withhold the unqualified recommendation and obtain updated evidence or use a conservative reversible response.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Held-out relevant observations confirm calibration and the intervention’s actual mechanism under the new conditions.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Invented scenario; contemporary simulation evidence motivates the assumption check but does not validate this intervention.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: A running declarative case has already performed an action that a newly added rule retrospectively forbids.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Check encoded history compatibility and have authorised actors adjudicate the real obligation rather than silently rewriting the trace.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Do not infer safe instance migration from syntactic validity. Retain the old case rule, negotiate an exception or resolve the obligation under a justified change policy.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: A valid history mapping and applicable rule semantics show the new constraint is not retroactive or the history is actually compatible.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Formal-model test under declared trace semantics; no universal legal conclusion follows.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: A small stable service already uses a clear shared note, an effective manager and direct recipient feedback.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Identify any consequential decision or controlled failure that a formal BPM suite would support better than the existing arrangement.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Record already addressed or simpler mechanism sufficient where no unmet function is found; do not prescribe a new platform or office.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Scale, turnover, complex dependencies or costly errors make the existing account inadequate.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Analytical test of omission; not proof that informal methods always dominate.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: The longitudinal workflow programme follows 25 intended processes but evaluates seven implemented processes.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Keep implementation and successful-process outcome denominators separate; inspect raw and modelled comparisons.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Retain conditional technical benefit while rejecting automatic adoption and uniform outcome claims.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: A broader independent contemporary study with credible comparisons could change transfer judgements.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Historical selected cohort; same programme as earlier reports; no universal failure percentage.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: The modelling-guidelines experiment finds no significant improvement on its tested outcomes.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Examine sample, task order, power and task/user scope.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Guideline compliance cannot stand in for demonstrated model quality; do not infer equivalence or universal uselessness.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Representative well-controlled replications may identify the conditions where guidelines help.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Student educational tasks; small sample and order effects.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: PF2 process records misfit some actual print work but support contractual accountability.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Identify both enactment and accounting consumers before removing supposedly ceremonial records.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Preserve useful accountability while repairing or decoupling the execution representation.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: The accountability consumer disappears or a cheaper equivalent account becomes sufficient.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Dourish reanalyses the earlier case; original 1995 text not accessed.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: The 2026 workaround-driven cycle investigates recurring goal/process misalignments.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Distinguish the workaround’s local usefulness from the best solution to its underlying cause.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Feed misalignment evidence into alternative redesigns rather than automatically make the workaround standard.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: Independent outcomes show the procedure adds cost without useful diagnosis or harms reporting.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Selected settings and related prior-case ancestry; no universal causal effect.

composition_tests.SCENARIO: Current-state simulation improves several comparisons but warm-up predicts remaining time better on BPIC17; finer uncertainty grouping can lose coverage.
composition_tests.DISCRIMINATING_TEST: Inspect unexplained delays, data/model scope and calibration rather than choosing the technically richer method by default.
composition_tests.COMPOSITION_JUDGEMENT: Use the simplest adequate state/error model and retain explicit failure conditions.
composition_tests.FALSIFIER_OR_REVISION_TRIGGER: New representative data or improved models may change the preferred forecast configuration.
composition_tests.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Retrospective as-is evaluation; not demonstrated what-if intervention success.

synthesis_exports.MECHANISM: Identify the intended result, its recipients and the end-to-end work that produces it. Make competing outcome claims visible before choosing measures or redesigning tasks; a purchaser’s preference is not automatically every affected person’s interest.
synthesis_exports.CRITERION: A proposed change can be judged against an explicit outcome and identified recipients, rather than only a department’s activity count.
